All three referred companies contacted me with a similar approach, based on an internet aerial photo of the property which was overlaid with their suggested number and arrangement of panels. Each followed up with a phone call, where Dan the Solar man differentiated themselves by asking sensible questions about my property before providing a solution (both other companies suggested inappropriate arrangements).  Their quote did not have limits on supply, such as "only 15m of cabling included" as part of their contract, and they were willing to negotiate key items of their contract to reach an agreement.  Their price was not the cheapest, through is was more 'all inclusive' than the others.  Dan the Solar Man sent an installer out to inspect the property to clarify panel arrangements and potential electrical switchboard issues prior to the contract.  They gave sufficient notice for the installation date, arrived promptly at the agreed time, and were professional (including wearing masks etc) at all times.  A supplier issue (inverter and electrical panel delivery) prevented the installation being completed in the one day, though they promptly arranged a follow-up date, again arrived on time, finished the installation, and advised the next steps (independent electrical inspection, account setup, distributor's electrical meter mode-change) and expected time frames clearly.  I'm now awaiting for the inspection and meter change, though now that the physical installation is complete, my review of Dan the Solar Man is that they were very good to deal with, and I would recommend them.
